The Haryana Civil Services has released the HPCS notification 2025 on January 30, 2026, in online mode, on the official website. The Commission will activate the HPCS application form 2026 from February 6, 2026. The last date to fill out the HPCS 2025 application form is February 26, 2026 (5:00 PM). Candidates who are interested in appearing for the exam have to pay the HPCS application fee 2025 before the closing of the application dates. The HPCS 2025 prelims exam will be held on April 26, 2026, for one day. Whereas the HPCS mains exam 2025 is scheduled to be conducted from June 27 to 29, 2026, for three days.
As per the official notification. The application fee was Rs. 1000 for the General male candidate, Rs. 250 for General female and all SC candidates. Candidates belonging to the PWD category will not have to pay the application fee. To be eligible for HCS, candidates must have a graduation degree (of any stream) from a recognised University with the required certificate/ documents, etc. issued on or before the application closing date. The age limit is between 21- 42 years old. However, candidates belonging to reserved categories will be provided upper age relaxation by the commission. The exam is conducted in three phases - Preliminary exam, Mains exam and Personal Interview. Only those candidates who qualify the prelims exam will be called for HCS Main exam. After qualifying the main exam (written), there will be a Personality Test (interview) carrying 75 marks.

Candidates must be graduates (Commerce, Science or Arts) from a recognised university as on the application closing date. They must possess all of their certificates and documents, in support of their educational qualification, before the application closing date. The HCS eligibility criteria also set an age limit of 21- 42 years. For the post of DSP, the age limit is 21- 27 years. However, the upper age limit has been stretched for certain categories of candidates belonging to Haryana, ex-military persons, etc.
The eligibility criteria of HCS Main exam is the same as the pre-exam. In addition to that, only those candidates who qualify the pre-exam will be eligible to appear for HCS Main exam. Candidates must note that since the pre-exam acts as a screening test, it is only a stepping stone towards being posted in the Haryana civil services. Marks scored in the pre-exam will not be counted in the final selection.
The HCS Preliminary exam pattern suggests that the exam will be conducted on offline mode. Candidates will have to attempt two papers- General Studies and an elective paper in which candidates will have to choose among 19 subjects. Both the papers will carry 100 marks and will last for a duration of 2 hours each. Questions will be objective with 5 answer options. Every correct response rewards 2 marks whereas every incorrect response deducts 0.25 mark.
The HCS Main exam will consist of 4 papers carrying 600 marks in total. The papers are in the following order- English, Hindi, General Studies, and two elective subjects. The exam pattern of HCS Main exam 2019 mentions that the paper will be objective in nature. Each question carries 2 marks and an incorrect response negates 0.25 mark. Candidates who clear this round will be eligible to appear for the Personality Test (interview) of 75 marks.

title: Rs 100 Crore Cyber Fraud Unearthed In Haryana, 66 Arrested - NDTV
Rs 150 crore fraud detected at Kotak Mahindra Bank's Panchkula branch, bank orders probe - IBTimes India
article_text:
A major financial irregularity has come to light in Haryana, where the Panchkula Municipal Corporation has found discrepancies of over Rs 150 crore in its fixed deposits with Kotak Mahindra Bank.
The development comes just a month after a Rs 590-crore fraud was reported at the Chandigarh branch of IDFC First Bank.
According to NDTV Profit report, the civic body had invested funds in fixed deposit receipts (FDRs) at the bank's Sector 11 branch.
However, the issue surfaced when the corporation requested the maturity amount of a Rs 58-crore deposit to be transferred into its account.
While bank records initially showed that the transfer had been completed, the money never reached the corporation.
A closer investigation revealed that the bank statement itself was fake, and the funds had allegedly been diverted into fraudulent accounts.
Officials later found that all the fixed deposits linked to this case were forged and that no actual money was present in the accounts, as per the report.
Reacting to the development, Kotak Mahindra Bank said it is cooperating with authorities and has started a detailed reconciliation of the fixed deposits and related accounts after being approached by the municipal corporation.
Officials said the total discrepancy could be over Rs 150 crore, and further details are expected to emerge as the probe progresses, the report stated.
Meanwhile, last month, another private lender IDFC First Bank had disclosed a Rs 590 crore fraud at its Chandigarh branch.
In an exchange filing on February 22, the private lender said that it will pursue strict disciplinary, civil and criminal action against the employees and other external individuals responsible, in accordance with applicable law.
However, on the same day, the Haryana Government de-empanelled IDFC First Bank and AU Small Finance Bank from handling government business with immediate effect after an alleged fraud of around Rs 590 crore came to light.

Haryana Relieves Consumers from Sharing Electricity Transformer Costs
The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) has announced a significant change to benefit the farming community. As of January 15, 2024, no fees will be charged for the replacement and repair of electricity transformers. This amendment to the Electricity Supply Code Regulations, 2014, aims to ease the financial burden on farmers.
Previously, consumers had to pay a portion of the cost for transformer replacement or repair. If a transformer was damaged or stolen during the warranty period, consumers were required to deposit 20% of the cost. Beyond the warranty period, they had to pay 10%. This policy predominantly affected agricultural connections.
Relief for Farmers
Farmers faced additional financial strain due to these costs, especially in cases of theft. The state government recognised the critical role farmers play in the economy and decided to alleviate their burden. The new regulation ensures that no fees will be charged for any reason, including theft.
An official statement highlighted that this move is in line with the state government's directions. The revised cost-sharing mechanism aims to provide much-needed relief to farmers who are already dealing with numerous challenges.
Impact on Agricultural Connections
The previous requirement for farmers to share the cost of replacing or repairing transformers added unnecessary financial pressure. By eliminating these fees, the government hopes to support farmers more effectively and enhance their economic stability.
The HERC's fourth amendment reflects a commitment to addressing the needs of the agricultural sector. This change is expected to have a positive impact on farmers, reducing their financial burdens and supporting their vital contributions to the state's economy.
This regulatory update underscores the government's recognition of farmers' importance and its efforts to provide them with necessary support. The elimination of fees for transformer replacement and repair is a step towards easing the financial challenges faced by the farming community.
The new regulation is part of broader efforts to support agriculture in Haryana. By removing these costs, the government aims to create a more favourable environment for farmers, helping them focus on their essential work without additional financial stress.
This initiative demonstrates a clear understanding of the difficulties faced by farmers and a commitment to providing practical solutions. The revised policy is expected to bring significant relief and support to those in the agricultural sector.
The decision aligns with broader state policies aimed at supporting agriculture and ensuring that farmers can continue their crucial work without undue financial hardship. This change marks an important step in recognising and addressing the needs of Haryana's farming community.

title: Brazilian photographer's mystery model who's Saraswati, Sweety, Seema in Haryana - India Today
article_text:
Brazilian photographer's mystery model who's Saraswati, Sweety, Seema in Haryana
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged electoral fraud in Haryana, showing the image of a woman featuring on 22 voter cards in Haryana. That photo turns out to be of a model photographed by Brazilian photographer Matheus Ferrero. Though the model's identity remains a mystery, her photo has long been circulated on stock image platforms and by news portals.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's press conference on Wednesday—meant to make major revelations about the alleged vote theft and irregularities in the electoral rolls—has sparked a search for a young woman whose photo appeared in multiple entries on the rolls in Haryana. "She voted 22 times in the last Haryana Assembly election," Rahul claimed.
"Who is this lady? What is her name? Where does she come from? But she voted 22 times in Haryana, at 10 different booths, and has multiple names: Seema, Sweety, Saraswati, Rashmi, Vilma...," said Rahul Gandhi, alleging that the image of the woman's image was used for several voters in Haryana.
"But turns out she is actually a Brazilian model," added Rahul Gandhi.
Though Rahul claimed that she was a Brazilian model, the truth is that the photo was clicked by a Brazilian photographer but the identity of the woman remains a mystery. It was Matheus Ferrero who actually clicked this model's photos way back in 2017.
A simple reverse image search on Google revealed that it was actually Ferrero who had clicked the photo of the model. Her name, however, has not been disclosed by him. These images of the model appear on major stock image platforms such as Unsplash and Pexels, with Ferrero shown as the owner of the intellectual property.
India Today Digital has reached out to photographer Matheus Ferrero, and this copy will be updated if and when he responds.
Image-hosting platform Unsplash actually features two images of the same model clicked by Ferrero in 2017. One is the photo that Rahul Gandhi alleged appeared on the Haryana voter IDs, and the second shows the same model in the same attire—a denim jacket over a white T-shirt, with hoop earrings—and against the same background. Two different shots, but clearly the same model.
On another free image hosting site, the caption for the image Rahul Gandhi showed, says, "Woman Wearing Blue Denim Jacket".
One of the two images clicked by Ferrero, which Rahul Gandhi claimed was used against the names of Seema, Sweety, Saraswati, Rashmi, and Vilma, has, since 2017, been used by various news outlets and skincare portals as a stock image.
The image has been used by websites for a wide range of content—from beauty and skincare tips, fashion and lifestyle stories, and motivational blogs to news features, social media posts, and even wellness and cosmetic treatment articles.
"You'll look beautiful even without makeup—just do this," a headline in Hindi said.
Not just that, several Facebook accounts with names of Indian women have also used this image as a profile photo.
Now, while it is known that the woman's photographer is Brazilian, the nationality of the model, claimed Brazilian by Rahul Gandhi, couldn't be verified.
Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday used the model's image as he doubled down on his vote chori (vote theft) allegations against the BJP and the Election Commission. He claimed massive voter fraud in the 2024 Haryana assembly elections.
He asserted, citing what he called "100% proof," that 25 lakh fake votes—roughly 12% of the state's electorate—were cast, alleging "systemic manipulation" intended to turn a Congress victory into defeat. However, Election Commission sources dismissed his claims, noting that no appeals had been filed against the state’s electoral rolls and that only 22 election petitions were pending in the Punjab and Haryana High Court out of 90 assembly seats, reflecting a limited legal challenge to the results. BJP leader and Union Minister Kiren Rijiju rubbished Rahul Gandhi's use of the model's image, referring to his earlier press conference when another woman, whose image the Congress leader had used, called him out.
So, in the latest scenario, though we know that the image that Rahul Gandhi said featured on 22 voter ID cards was clicked by Brazilian photographer, Matheus Ferrero, but her identity and nationality remain a mystery.

title: Every paisa will be returned: Haryana CM vows action in Rs 590-crore IDFC fraud - India Today
article_text:
Every paisa will be returned: Haryana CM vows action in Rs 590-crore IDFC fraud
A major financial scandal has surfaced involving a suspected Rs 590 crore fraud in Haryana government accounts at a private bank. The Chief Minister assures strict action and full recovery of public funds as investigations proceed.
A suspected Rs 590 crore fraud involving government accounts at a private bank has rocked the state, with Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini promising that “every paisa will be returned” and warning that no one involved will be spared.
The controversy erupted after IDFC First Bank disclosed in a regulatory filing that unauthorised and fraudulent activities were detected at its Chandigarh branch in accounts linked to Haryana government entities.
A day after the disclosure, the issue reverberated in the Assembly on February 23, with the opposition demanding answers and the government announcing a formal investigation.
HOW THE FRAUD SURFACED
The matter came to light when a Haryana government department sought closure of its account and transfer of funds to another bank. During the process, discrepancies were noticed between the amount mentioned and the actual balance available.
“In the process, certain discrepancies were observed in the amount mentioned vis-a-vis the balance in the account,” the bank said in its filing.
Similar irregularities were subsequently detected in other accounts of Haryana government entities that had been operating through the same Chandigarh branch. According to the bank, the suspected fraud is currently estimated at Rs 590 crore, though it added that a reconciliation exercise is under way to determine the final figure after validation of claims and recoveries.
“Prima facie, unauthorised and fraudulent activities have been carried out by certain employees at a particular branch in Chandigarh in a specific set of Haryana state government accounts and potentially involving other individuals/entities/counterparties,” the filing said.
The bank maintained that the issue is confined to “a specific group of government-linked accounts within Haryana Government” handled through the Chandigarh branch and does not extend to other customers.
GOVERNMENT’S RESPONSE IN ASSEMBLY
Raising the issue in the House, Leader of the Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda questioned the government’s response and asked what action had been initiated.
Hooda said the bank had detected the irregularities and demanded clarity from the government on its next steps.
Responding to the debate, Saini told the Assembly that a probe has been ordered and that both the State Anti-Corruption Bureau and vigilance authorities are investigating the matter.
“Be it a bank employee or any government employee, anyone who is found involved will not be spared,” Saini said.
He added that once discrepancies were detected, the government immediately moved to transfer the funds to another bank.
“The government is taking this issue seriously, be it bank employee or any other employee, anyone who is involved, strict action will be taken,” he told the House.
“We are investigating the matter very seriously. The ACB is investigating it. Our government works in a transparent manner. It is not an issue which we will take lightly.”
BANK FILES COMPLAINT, INFORMS REGULATOR
In its filing, IDFC First Bank said it has informed the banking regulator and lodged a police complaint. The bank described the case as involving unauthorised transactions carried out by certain employees at the Chandigarh branch in collusion with other parties.
The Haryana government has since de-empanelled the bank for government business with immediate effect, Saini confirmed in the Assembly.
As the probe gathers pace, the focus remains on tracing the flow of funds and fixing accountability. For now, the Chief Minister’s message was unambiguous: those responsible will face action and public money will be recovered.

title: HC upholds selection of Haryana police inspectors in 2009, dismisses fraud claims - The Times of India
article_text:
Chandigarh: Upholding the 2009 selection of police inspectors by Haryana Staff Selection Commission (HSSC) during former CM
Bhupinder Singh Hooda's term, the Punjab and Haryana high court ruled that "there was no fraud, suppression of facts, or connivance by candidates or the selection commission".
According to HC, in the absence of illegalities, it is not possible to set aside the selection of candidates who have been working with the state police for the last 15 years and have been promoted from the post of inspector to deputy superintendent of police (DSP).
"Cancellation of their selection would be worse than the alleged irregularities. It is well-known that solutions cannot be worse than the problem," the HC stated in its order released on Monday.
While dismissing the petition filed by Amit Kumar and others, Justice Jagmohan Bansal concluded that "there were irregularities, but no illegality was committed".
The petition was filed in 2011, wherein Amit Kumar, a candidate who applied for the post of inspector (male) in Haryana Police in response to an advertisement on July 22, 2008, approached the HC pleading that he was a meritorious candidate, having scored 145 out of 200 marks in the written examinations, and had obtained the second-highest marks in the general category. However, in the interview, he was given only seven marks, and the selected candidates, who had links with the political dispensation, were given extraordinary marks, i.e., 18 to 22 out of 25, only to ensure that they came into the zone of consideration for appointment to the post.
The petitioner also provided a list of selected candidates and their political connections. Some more unsuccessful candidates also filed petitions on the issue.
The allegations included the use of fluid on the answer sheet, filling in wrong information, and not signing of answer sheet by successful candidates. It was also alleged that the interview marks per candidate were filled up by one person alone, whereas the interview was conducted by two persons, and both ought to have signed the marks sheet of the viva voce.

title: Two Gurugram sub-tehsils under lens for registry ‘fraud’ - The Tribune
article_text:
Sanjay Yadav
Gurugram, June 10
A major registry fraud may come to the fore at Kadipur and Harsaru sub-tehsils of Gurugram district as registration was allegedly done at rates lower than the circle rate in these two sub-tehsils. This has come to light in a survey conducted by the Income Tax (I-T) Department on Friday.
The Income Tax Department was not even being informed about registries by both sub-tehsils for the past five years. That’s why the survey was conducted by the I-T Department.
DC Nishant Kumar Yadav confirmed that this matter is being investigated. “I came to know that data was not transferred to the I-T department due to some technical error in software. The I-T Department has taken the data for analysis,” added DC Yadav.
The I-T Department will issue notices to officials of both sub-tehsils under Section 50C of the Income Tax Act which considers the value adopted by the stamp valuation authority (SVA) to impose stamp duty on property registration as a guide to determine whether the land/building in the sale agreement is undervalued.
In the survey by the Income Tax Department, it was revealed that in the past five years, more than one lakh registries were done in Kadipur and Harsaru sub-tehsils.
Out of these, 10,000 registries were for sold and bought property and 90,000 registries were for transfer, sale deed, lease etc.
In the past five years, 10,000 registries worth more than Rs 30 lakh were found.
As per rules, information about registries of over Rs 30 lakh was to be given to the Income Tax Department, but the information was not shared by both the sub-tehsil offices. In such a situation, the possibility of irregularities and loss of government revenue cannot be ruled out.
According to a senior official of the I-T Department, the records have been taken from Kadipur and Harsaru and their checking has started. “First of all, we will check all the registries which were done at a low circle rate. The team will determine how much income tax has been evaded. Then, the process of income tax recovery will be started by the department. Besides this, the information of revenue will also be shared with the government,” he added.
The official added that the other tehsils of Gurugram are also on the department’s radar. There are many flaws in the tehsils from which information is being shared with the Income Tax Department. So, the Income Tax Department will collect information by conducting surveys in other tehsils of the district as well.
Ashish Malik, Naib Tehsildar of Harsaru sub-tehsil, denied any wrongdoing. He said that there was a technical issue in the software and due to it, details of Aadhaar and PAN cards of buyers and sellers were not submitted to the I-T Department.
“There is no irregularity and any type of revenue loss. The information was not submitted to the I-T Department only due to technical issues in the software. We have also written a letter to the National Information Centre (NIC) demanding an update in software. Before 2020, PAN card was not mandatory. But now, it is mandatory for all registries of more than Rs 10 lakh. The IT Department will release the survey report soon and we will ensure the automatic provision in the registries soon,” Malik said.

Morni Hills demarcation: HC imposes Rs 20K cost on Haryana over delayed application - The Times of India
article_text:
Panchkula: The Punjab and Haryana high court sought clarification from the Haryana govt regarding the survey and demarcation of nearly 45 acres of land in Morni Hills, while imposing a cost of Rs 20,000 on the state for filing a delayed application.
The direction came during the hearing of a case filed by advocate Vijay Bansal, where the state sought exemption from the personal appearance of the forest and wildlife department secretary. The court accepted the application but directed the state to deposit the cost with the Poor Patients Welfare Fund at PGIMER, Chandigarh.
The court observed that the application indicated that survey and demarcation work in Morni Hills was already completed before April 16. It has now asked the applicant's counsel to verify and clarify the correctness of these claims. The matter is listed for further hearing on May 15.

The court also ordered that all non-forest activities in the Morni Hills area remain prohibited until the final notification is issued.
However, the court later noted delays in compliance. Instead of proceeding as directed, the Haryana govt reconstituted the FSO into a three-member panel in Sept 2025 without seeking prior approval from the court. The court expressed concern over the delay and even initiated contempt proceedings against the Forest Secretary earlier this year for non-compliance with its orders.
The ongoing proceedings are part of the court's continued monitoring to ensure timely protection and legal status of forest land in the ecologically sensitive Morni Hills region.

title: I-T lens on property deals worth Rs 28k crore in Haryana’s Manesar - The Times of India

Over the past five years, the tehsil office registered property deals worth an estimated Rs 28,000 crore. But in a glaring breach, the Permanent Account Number (PAN) of buyers and sellers, which is a must for transactions above Rs 30 lakh, was missing from records.
The survey conducted by a 10-member team over 24 hours found that the registration software used at the tehsil failed to capture PAN details, despite existing norms requiring tehsil offices to share names, PAN, and Aadhaar numbers with the income tax department for all high-value property deals.
The problem isn't confined to Manesar. The survey revealed that the protocol was not being followed in 93 tehsils across 22 districts. An I-T official explained that while PAN cards were collected during the registration process, they were not being entered into the system, reportedly because of software glitches.
The omission of PAN details raised red flags about the transparency and legality of these transactions.
Officials said without PAN data, authorities cannot track the flow of money and identify possible tax evasion.
"Even if 1% of people evade taxes, the amount would be huge," an I-T official said, spotlighting the scale of potential revenue loss
Previous surveys at Wazirabad and Kadipur tehsils had revealed similar irregularities, suggesting a broader pattern of negligence or systemic failure in the registration process.
Officials said the I-T department had alerted revenue officials and urged them to update the software and ensure compliance with documentation rules.
District revenue officer Vijay Yadav confirmed that the survey at Manesar tehsil focused on registries completed over the past five years. "Irregularities were found in feeding buyer and seller identity cards and PAN details into the software. This will be rectified," he said.
The I-T department is now working to trace the PAN of those involved in these property transactions and will cross-check whether the corresponding income is reflected in their tax returns.
The outcome of this exercise could have far-reaching implications, not only for those involved but also for the credibility of the property registration system in the region.
According to officials, the survey was part of the state govt's efforts to curb corruption and irregularities in property registrations. In recent years, the system has been made paperless to enhance transparency. However, the failure to feed PAN details into the digital system undermines these reforms and opens the door to fraudulent practices.

SIR in Haryana: State to verify voter list by October 20
Haryana's CEO A Sreenivas announced a new voter list will be prepared by October 20, 2024, with BLOs matching current and 2002 lists for accuracy.
Haryana chief electoral officer (CEO) A Sreenivas on Monday said that, as per the Election Commission of India (ECI) guidelines, a new voter list will be prepared and all booth level officers (BLOs) will be tasked with matching the current voter list of Haryana with that of the year 2002 by October 20 this year.
If a voter’s name appears in both lists, no additional documents will be required. Sreenivas said that both the 2002 and 2024 voter lists are available on the department’s website for public access.
The CEO has appealed to all registered voters, eligible youth, and political party representatives to cooperate in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) aimed at creating an error-free voter list.
Sreenivas also directed district election officers (DEOs) across the state to fill vacant BLO positions and issue their identity cards to ensure smooth progress in preparing the new voter list. He also issued directions to give training to officers and employees related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
On September 10, the ECI had organised a meeting of CEOs of all states, giving directions to implement SIR across the country. Following the meeting, Haryana’s CEO conducted a video conference with DEOs and electoral registration officers (EROs) regarding SIR implementation.
As part of the process, BLOs will visit every voter’s home to collect data for the new voter list. Voters will fill out two copies of an enumeration form—one for themselves and the other for the BLO to prepare the list.
Sreenivas stated that, as per ECI guidelines, polling stations will be rationalised based on a maximum of 1,200 voters per station. If a station exceeds this limit, a new polling station will be created.
Additionally, the CEO directed that regular meetings be held with representatives from all recognised national and state political parties, and that the list of booth level agents be obtained. Timely printing and distribution of enumeration sheets to BLOs should also be ensured.

IT dept detects Rs 1000 crore racket in Haryana post-demonetisation - The New Indian Express
article_text:
CHANDIGARH: The Investigation Wing of Income Tax (North West Region) unearthed a hawala racket of more than Rs 1000 crore in the small town of Charkhi Dadri in Haryana since demonetisation. Additionally, undisclosed income to the tune of Rs 283 crore was also seized in the region.
Director general (investigations) of Income Tax (North West Region) Madhu Mahajan said that numerous hawala accommodation entry operators have stepped up their operations in the region post demonetisation. These rackets take cash and enable money to move from one bank to another on a real time and gross basis for a commission. Also, to launder the unaccounted cash, Benami accounts were opened by the gangs.
“In one interesting case of Charkhi Dadri in Haryana, more than Rs 1000 crore was found to be laundered and of this over Rs 100 crore may belong to the people of Punjab. A man in his thirties had printed a few letter pads of ‘fake’ companies and he, along with his associates opened several bank accounts in various branches of both nationalised and private banks across the country to facilitate these illegal operations,’’ she said.
Describing the modus operandi, principal director of Income Tax (investigation) Parneet Singh Sachdev said, “The people who were affected by the demonetisation move of the government got in touch with him to convert their black money into white for about 20 percent commission. The money used to be deposited in various bank accounts, which is not possible without the connivance of bank officials and then money was transferred through RTGC from one account to the other so that it could not be detected. Finally, the original owner received the money in his or her account.’’
“People have also taken loans from him in order to convert their black income into white. He had also given fake bills of various purchases so that the money could be accounted for. Already, more than 18 beneficiaries have been detected. His account which had more Rs 10 crore at the time of his arrest was sealed immediately. Also, we have updated CBI and Enforcement Directorate regarding this case,’’ he said.
Madhu Mahajan said undisclosed income to the tune of Rs 283 crore was also detected in the region during the last fifteen surveys.
“Till date, 63 cases have been referred to the Enforcement Directorate. We found that some banks, especially cooperative banks were not following the standard operation procedures of RBI, as accounts were not properly maintained. We have seized cash of more than Rs. 2.5 crore from cooperative banks and helper companies. Helper companies are those which are entrusted with carrying cash to ATMs.”

title: Educated youth struggle for jobs across Punjab, Haryana, Himachal - The Times of India
article_text:
Chandigarh: Youth unemployment in Punjab and Himachal Pradesh is nearly double the national average, with educated young people bearing the brunt of a deepening jobs crisis, according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (Jan–Dec 2025).
Unemployment in the 15–29 age group stands at 19.8% in Himachal Pradesh and 17% in Punjab, far above the national average of 9.9%. Haryana records 11.8%, also above the all-India level but significantly lower than its neighbouring states.
The data points to a widening gap between rising education levels and limited job opportunities. With a large pool of diploma holders, graduates and postgraduates, the region is struggling to absorb its educated workforce, while a sharp gender divide persists, with young women facing significantly higher unemployment.
Overall unemployment in the 15–59 age group is also above the national average in all three states. Punjab records 5.8%, Himachal Pradesh 5.2% and Haryana 4.7%, against 3.4% nationally.
Despite higher education levels in the region, graduate unemployment stands at 11.6% in Punjab, 10.3% in Haryana and 12.1% in Himachal Pradesh, compared with 11.2% nationally. Postgraduate unemployment is also high at 9.4% in Punjab, 9.6% in Haryana and 11.0% in Himachal Pradesh, against 10.0% nationally.
The share of population with secondary education and above is 59.6% in Himachal Pradesh, 52.5% in Haryana and 49% in Punjab, all significantly above the national average of 42.4%.
A closer look at higher educational attainment shows a substantial pool of qualified youth. Diploma or certificate holders account for 5.9% in Himachal Pradesh and 3.2% in Haryana, both higher than Punjab at 1.4%, which is at par with the national average. Graduate-level education is recorded at 12.8% in Haryana, 10.8% in Himachal Pradesh and 8.7% in Punjab, compared with 10.8% nationally. Postgraduate and above qualification levels are also higher in the region, with 6.0% in Himachal Pradesh and 5.3% in Haryana, against 2.8% in Punjab and 3.3% nationally.
GENDER DISPARITY
Among young women aged 15–29 years, unemployment stands at 27.7% in Punjab and 17.4% in Himachal Pradesh, both higher than the national figure of 11.3%. Haryana's figure is 14.3%.
The Worker Population Ratio for the 15–29 age group also reflects limited job absorption. Only 39% of youth in Punjab and 35% in Haryana are working, compared with 41.4% nationally. Himachal Pradesh records 44.9%, marginally above the national average.
Participation levels also show sharp differences. The Labour Force Participation Rate among youth is 47.0% in Punjab, close to the national average of 46.0%. Haryana records a lower participation rate of 39.7%, suggesting a significant share of youth are outside the labour market. Himachal Pradesh, at 56.0%, shows higher participation but also elevated unemployment, indicating that many young people are actively seeking work but unable to find jobs.
EMPLOYMENT NATURE VARIES
The nature of employment also varies across the three states. Himachal Pradesh relies heavily on self-employment, with 67.6% of workers in this category, compared with 44.5% in Punjab and 44.0% in Haryana. Regular salaried jobs are more common in Punjab and Haryana, at 36.2% and 39.4%, respectively, compared with 23.2% in Himachal Pradesh and 23.6% nationally.

title: Rs 4.5 cr property tax scam in Panipat MC - The Tribune
article_text:
A scam of Rs 4.5 crore in the property tax branch of the Panipat Municipal Corporation has come to light. The scam was unearthed after the Joint Commissioner noticed his official ID allegedly being wrongly used by his personal assistant (PA) in correction of property IDs, property tax and issuance of no-dues certificate (NDC).
Following reports of an inquiry, the services of the personnel assistant of the Joint Commissioner were terminated. The MC also wrote to the police to register a criminal case and to probe the matter in detail.
The Yashi Company had conducted the survey of properties and the data was uploaded on the portal in October 2022. But discrepancies were found in over 70,000 properties in the data.
Then, the MC launched several campaigns to correct the property IDs. After that, the property IDs were made mandatory for the registration of property. If anyone wanted to purchase property, the no-dues certificate (NDC) from the MC was mandatory and the property should be in an approved area.
Sources said the property ID correction, wrong tax bill correction, issuing NDC and other property tax-related works were with Joint Commissioner Sanjay Kumar.
But his personnel assistant (PA), a woman employee under Haryana Kaushal Rozgar Nigam (HKRN), reportedly in connivance with some other employees and agents active in the Municipal Corporation and Tehsil office reportedly started clearing files by using the official ID of the Joint Commissioner without official approval and physical verification. The unauthorised zeroing of property tax outstanding against the properties led to a loss of over Rs 4.5 crore to the Panipat MC, sources said.
As the matter came to light, Sanjay Kumar filed a complaint with the MC Commissioner following which the Commissioner ordered a detailed inquiry into the matter and a special committee comprising Additional Commissioner Vivek Chaudhary, Mani Tyagi, Joint Commissioner and expert members was formed.
It was revealed in the inquiry that around 400 files were cleared by the PA during her tenure. Of these, 325 files were cleared wrongly and property tax of Rs 4.5 crore was made zero, a senior official said. Also, fake property IDs were created of properties in unapproved areas by linking those with some property in approved area and NDC was issued to register the property.
Even in the register, the PA and her associates entered the wrongly passed files, the sources said.
Dr Pankaj Yadav, Commissioner, MC, said that the PA misused the official ID of Joint Commissioner Sanjay Kumar and cleared the files without any official approval in connivance with some agents and officials.
She was suspended when the matter came to light and now, her services have been terminated, the Commissioner said. The property tax which was wrongly zeroed has been reverted and now, tax is outstanding against those properties. Now, notices would be served to all these property owners, he said. “It is a nexus between some officials and agents active in the MC and Tehsil office. To break this nexus, we have written to the police to lodge a case and to probe the matter,” the Commissioner said.

title: UP set to erect 501 pillars to mark 65km border with Haryana - The Times of India
article_text:
Noida: The district administration has started installing state boundary pillars along the 65km stretch of UP-Haryana border that falls in GB Nagar, following a detailed ground survey in 32 villages earlier this year.
Officials said a total of 501 boundary pillars are to be erected along this stretch of the inter-state border.
The move is part of a broader inter-state demarcation exercise across five UP districts — Saharanpur, Shamli, Baghpat, GB Nagar, and Aligarh — where the Yamuna river forms the natural boundary with Haryana.
"In many areas, Yamuna's changing course causes agricultural land to shift from one state's side to the other, leading to repeated ownership claims and disputes. Erection of fixed boundary markers will help avoid such issues and bring clarity to land records," said additional district magistrate (judicial) Bhair Pal Singh.
In March, TOI had reported that officials carried out a drive to verify and formalise land ownership in 32 villages along the disputed border.
District magistrate Manish Verma issued survey slips to 3,000 landowners from five villages in the first phase, as a mark of land ownership confirmation. The demarcation project spans 132 villages across the five UP districts, affecting over 11,200 hectares of land.
On the Haryana side, the six impacted districts are Yamuna Nagar, Karnal, Panipat, Sonipat, Faridabad, and Palwal.

title: Haryana: Now, drones & satellite imagery to keep check on illegal mining - The Times of India
article_text:
GURUGRAM: The
Haryana chief secretary has directed all the deputy commissioners (DCs) of the state to carry out drone surveys, satellite imagery and videography of areas prone to illegal mining to get the actual ground status and find out changes, if any, due to illegal mining.
Illegal mining has again come into the limelight after the murder of Tauru DSP Surender Singh Bishnoi, allegedly by the mining mafia in Nuh.
It is rampant in the Aravalis despite a blanket ban on mining by the Supreme Court in 2009.
The eco-sensitive hill range was quarried relentlessly for decades for sand and stones used in construction before the ban. Cases of illegal mining are still reported from Gurugram, Faridabad, Rewari, Nuh and Mahendergarh districts.
Mining officer Anil Kumar said there is complete ban of mining in Gurugram and no permission has been given for any mining activity. The city has two crusher zones at Naurangpur and Raisina. Between January and August this year, 35 vehicles have been seized and 23 FIRs registered for illegal mining. "In addition, fines amounting to a total of Rs 56.9 lakh were imposed for illegal mining," he said.
Chief secretary of Haryana Sanjeev Kaushal on Wednesday held a meeting of all DCs through video conferencing over illegal mining and directed the DCs to use drones and videography to stop illegal mining.
Gurugram DC Nishant Yadav, DCP Upashana, mining officer Anil Kumar and other officials were present in the meeting.
The chief secretary briefed the officials about the standard operating procedure (SOP) prepared by the mines and geology department after the Tauru DSP's murder. He will conduct a district-wise review of steps taken to check mining in each district.
The SOP stresses on the use of drones, satellite imagery and videography of the areas prone to illegal mining. A district level task force under the deputy commissioner has been notified in all districts. "Drones and satellite imagery, along with videography, will be used to check illegal mining," Gurugram DC Nishant Yadav said.
Kaushal directed DCs to hold regular meetings of the district task force. A DCP, mining officer and officials of the Haryana Pollution Control Board, forest department and RTO will be members of the committee, which will identify areas prone to illegal mining. Members of the panel will visit these areas twice a month and make video recordings, while Haryana Space Application Centre (HARSAC) will provide satellite imagery and analytics on mining.
According to the SOP, in case of repeated instances of illegal mining, the DC can invoke Section 144 of the CrPC. The committee is expected to ensure checkpoints on roads leading to illegal mining affected areas for round the clock checking and surveillance.
Complaints on illegal mining will be brought to the notice of the DC and the mining officer. All licensed mineral dealers or screening plants will have to submit proof of original purchase bills, along with the list of vehicles used in transportation, on demand by the mines and geology department. No contractor will sell minerals without a bill, and only GPS-fitted vehicles will be allowed to carry these from the contracted area.
The disastrous impact of mining on the Aravalis has been seen in neighbouring Rajasthan, where 31 out of 128 hills in the Aravali region disappeared over a period of 50 years due to quarrying, according to findings of a Supreme Court-appointed central empowered committee in 2018.
Haryana has a total of 119 mines, of which 61 are lying vacant and 49 are operational at present. Most of the active mines are in Yamunanagar, Charkhi Dadri, Mahendergarh and Bhiwani. In Gurugram , Faridabad and Nuh, mining stopped officially after the 2009 order of the Supreme Court.

title: Haryana lost 14sqkm of forests in 2 yrs, Gurgaon saw a marginal increase - The Times of India
article_text:
Gurgaon: Haryana's forest cover decreased by almost 14sqkm in 2023 compared to 2021, according to a report released by the Forest Survey of India. In 2021, the state had a forest cover of 1,628.2sqkm, which reduced to 1,614.2sqkm in 2023.
The Indian State of Forest Report (ISFR), released on Saturday by environment and forest minister Bhupender Yadav, indicated that the reduction in forest cover in the state includes a decrease of 11.2sqkm in areas outside recorded forest areas (RFA) and a reduction of 2.8sqkm inside RFA. This totals a forest cover loss of almost 14sqkm, equivalent to 1,396 hectares.
Meanwhile, Haryana witnessed an increase in overall tree cover. In 2021, the state's total tree cover was 1,551.9sqkm, which increased to 1,793sqkm in 2023, a change in areas of 141.3sqkm. Tree cover is defined by all tree patches of the size less than 1 hectare occurring outside of the recorded forest area.
The report also indicates that 14 districts experienced a decline in forest cover, with Rohtak seeing the highest decrease at 4.3sqkm, followed by Mewat (4.1 sqkm), Hisar (1.9 sqkm), Bhiwani (1.9 sqkm), Mahendragarh (1.7 sqkm), Kurukshetra (1.6 sqkm), Panchkula (1.4 sqkm), Faridabad (1.1 sqkm), Charkhi Dadri (1.2 sqkm), Kaithal (1.3 sqkm), Rewari (0.5 sqkm), Panipat (0.5 sqkm), Fatehabad (0.3 sqkm), Palwal (0.2 sqkm), and Sonipat (0.1 sqkm).
To put this into perspective, one sqkm equals 100 hectares. Therefore, Rohtak lost 428 hectares, and Faridabad lost 108 hectares of forest. Meanwhile, Gurgaon's total forest area now stands at 113.1sqkm, an increase of 15 hectares from 2021.
It is notable that the current assessment shows an increase of 156.4sqkm in forest cover at the national level compared to the previous assessment. The report also highlighted that between 2011 and 2021, an area of 40,709.2sqkm was identified where forest density degraded, transitioning from very dense forest (VDF) and moderately dense forest (MDF) to open forest (OF) across India. In Haryana, this degradation occurred in 2,775 polygons, covering 34.1sqkm.
Additionally, the degradation from VDF, MDF, and OF to scrub reveals that 369,376 polygons, covering an area of 5,573sqkm, have been affected across India. These areas are categorised into three classes based on size: 0 to 10 hectares, 10 to 50 hectares, and over 50 hectares. "The identification of these areas followed a systematic process. The change polygons were converted from raster to vector format to achieve better overlay with other GIS layers of the states and to enrich the vector layer with more attribute values. This approach ensures a more detailed and accurate analysis of forest cover changes," the report stated.
According to the forest officials, the decline in forest cover is because of the diversion of land for non-forestry purposes under Forest Conservation Act. "Development projects such as roads have taken away large chunks of forest land across Haryana. In the coming years, more areas will be converted into non-forestry areas because of the upcoming road expansion projects," said a Haryana forest official. The report indicates a marginal increase in Haryana's forest cover over the decade. In 2013, Haryana had 1,583.4sqkm of forest cover, which increased to 1,614.2sqkm in 2023, reflecting a change of 30.9sqkm or 1.95%, but lower than the national average. Nationally, India's forest cover grew from 698,712.4sqkm in 2013 to 715,342.6sqkm in 2023, an increase of 16,630.3sqkm or 2.35%.
Experts expressed concerns about the accuracy of the data. "There are areas in Haryana recorded as forest, but they lack tree cover, such as the Gurgaon-Alwar road and Gurgaon-Pataudi road. This discrepancy needs to be highlighted in the report. The govt should provide details of areas officially recorded as forest but without trees," said RP Balwan, former conservator of forests (south Haryana).
"The 15-hectare increase in Gurgaon is only possible if it includes areas recently designated as forest, which already has forest features. Otherwise, the city, which hasn't seen significant enhancement in conversion, cannot show a positive trend in forest cover."
Debadityo Sinha, lead for climate and ecosystems at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, said, "The report highlights concerning trends in Haryana's forests. Scrub forest areas have increased by 11sqkm, and non-forest areas are also expanding, indicating significant land-use changes and forest degradation. The most severe degradation is observed in forest cover outside recorded forest areas. The state's forest cover are severely infested with non-native exotic tree species," he said.

title: Fingerprints cloned from sale deeds used to siphon money off bank accounts, warns Haryana police - ThePrint
article_text:
Chandigarh, May 12 (PTI) Fraudsters are cloning thumb impressions from sale deeds available on a Haryana government website and siphoning money off bank accounts, the state police has warned the land records department.
In a letter to the director of the state’s land records department dated May 10, the police said, “It is in reference to a case which has been traced by Faridabad police related to a Aadhaar-Enabled Payment System (AEPS) fraud where the victim’s money was withdrawn by creating a forged biometric thumb impression.” The fraudsters log on to the Jamabandi website, fill in district and tehsil details and random dates, and then download all sale deeds for that day, the police stated.
“From any of the registered sale deeds, they copy the thumb impression on a butter paper and then create duplicate silicone thumbs. These thumb impressions and other details are then used to withdraw money from Aadhaar-linked accounts using AEPS-enabled PoS machines,” the letter read.
Jamabandi is a document prepared as part of a record-of-right in every revenue estate. It contains entries regarding ownership, cultivation and various rights in land among others.
The Haryana Police communication further said, “Since many frauds are happening in this manner because of easy availability of thumb impressions and other details on sale deeds, it is highly recommended that only the first page of deeds are made visible for the general public.” The police also recommended an audit of the website to identify and fix other loopholes.
Last year too, the Haryana Police had claimed to have busted a gang allegedly siphoning off money from bank accounts of people using AEPS by cloning fingerprints.
AEPS is an NPCI-led model which allows online interoperable financial inclusion transactions at PoS (micro ATM) through the business correspondent of any bank using Aadhaar authentication.
The only inputs required to do a transaction under the AEPS mode are IIN (identification of the customer’s bank), Aadhaar number and fingerprint. PTI SUN IJT

title: Downloaded copies of bail order sufficient for immediate release, no need to wait for certified copy: Punjab & Haryana HC - SCC Online
article_text:
Punjab and Haryana High Court: An application was filed by a convict in a kidnapping case, under Section 430 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (‘BNSS’), seeking suspension of sentence in First Information Report under Sections 364-A, 307, 379-B and 482 read with Section 34 of the Penal Code, 1860 (‘IPC’). The Division Bench of Anoop Chitkara and Mandeep Pannu JJ. allowed the same and held that a downloaded copy of a bail or suspension of sentence order is sufficient for securing the release of an accused. The Court further clarified that when the certified copy of the order is not immediately provided by the Registry, the downloaded copy must be accepted by the Court before whom the bail bonds are furnished.
Background
In the present case, the convict had kidnapped the nephew of the complainant and had demanded Rs 50,000 as ransom. The complainant had given Rs 20,000 to them at the decided location. However, the complainant was told that his nephew had been shot in the foot and was thrown somewhere at Bhondsi Jail Road.
Upon searching the location concerned, the complainant could not trace his nephew. During investigation, the convictwere arrested and admitted their guilt. In pursuance of their disclosure statements, Rs 8000 and Rs 7500 were recovered from their respective places. Eventually, the nephew was found to be thrown near Sector 62, Baba Building Material, Gurugram in an injured condition.
The division Bench of this Court had stayed the recovery of the fine during the pendency of the appeal, and the said order was continuing till date and admitted the appeal for final hearing.
As per the custody certificate, the convict’s custody in the above FIR was 8 years, 3 months, and 5 days.
Analysis and Decision
The Court opined that the grounds to suspend the sentence of convict are sufficient considering:
- the time which was likely to take for the turn of this appeal for actual hearing,
- the amount of ransom being Rs. 50,000 coupled with the gun shot injury on leg, which was a non-vital part of the body, and
-
the convict’s custody of more than 8 years 3 months with remission and more than 7 years and 1 month without remission.
Therefore, the Court suspended the execution of sentence of imprisonment till further orders. Further, the Court held that the convict be released on bail, subject to furnishing bonds to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
The Court further observed that to ensure that every person in judicial custody who had been granted bail or whose sentence had been suspended got back their liberty without any delay, it was appropriate that whenever the bail order or the orders of suspension of sentence were not immediately sent by the Registry, computer systems, or Public Prosecutor, then in such a situation, to facilitate the immediate restoration of the liberty granted by any Court, the downloaded copies of all such orders, subject to verification, must be accepted by the Court before whom the bail bonds are furnished.
Furthermore, the Court held that there would be no need for a certified copy of this order for furnishing bonds, and any advocate for the convict can download this order along with case status from the official web page of this Court and attest it to be a true copy. If the attesting officer wants to verify the authenticity, such an officer can also verify it and may download and use the downloaded copy for attesting bonds.
[Amit Rana v. State of Haryana, 2025 SCC OnLine P&H 5348, decided on 5-8-2025]

title: Driving Licence in Haryana: Online and Offline Application Process - ACKO Drive
article_text:
Types of DL in Haryana
Different Driving Licences (DL) are granted in Haryana according to the kind of vehicle the applicant plans to drive. An outline of the various kinds of driver's licences that are available is provided below:
Learner's Licence (LL)
In the DL procedure, a learner's licence is the initial phase. This temporary licence is given to people learning to drive and is good for six months. During this time, the holder can prepare for the driving test needed to obtain a permanent licence and practice driving under specific limits.
Permanent Driving Licence (DL)
Those who pass the driving test and successfully maintain a learner's licence for at least 30 days can obtain a permanent driver's licence (DL), enabling them to drive on public roads independently.
Commercial Driving Licence (CDL)
Drivers who operate trucks, buses, and taxis must have a commercial driver's licence (DL). The eligibility requirements are more intensive because CDL is responsible for operating heavier trucks.
International Driving Permit (IDP)
In nations that recognise the IDP, Indian citizens are permitted to drive with an International Driving Permit. This is a valuable document for foreigners and tourists.
How to Apply for a Driving Licence (Online/Offline) in Haryana
You must first receive a learner's licence to apply for a DL in Haryana. You can apply for a permanent licence once you pass the driving exam. The process can be finished offline or online, offering ease and flexibility.
How to Apply for a DL Online in Haryana
Applying online offers the convenience of managing the application from home. Here’s how to do it:
- Step 1: Visit the official portal of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
- Step 2: Once on the website, select "Haryana" from the drop-down menu to proceed with the application.
- Step 3: Applying for a Learner’s Licence
- Step 4: Complete the application for a learner's licence by entering personal information, including name, residence, birth date, and blood type.
- Step 5: Choose a date for the learner's licence test and upload scanned copies of the necessary paperwork, including proof of address and age.
- Step 6: Confirm your reservation for the learner's test by paying the necessary application cost online.
- Step 7: Take the learner's test, which assesses your understanding of traffic laws, road signs, and safety procedures, at the selected RTO on the appointed day.
- Step 8: The learner's licence, which can be downloaded or obtained by email, will be issued if you pass. It will also be delivered to your address on file if you request it.
- Step 9: After holding the learner’s licence for at least 30 days, you can apply for a permanent licence by filling out Form 4 and paying the required fee online.
- Step 10: Choose a date for the driving test conducted at the RTO.
- Step 11: On the scheduled date, visit the RTO with your vehicle for the driving test. This test includes various components, such as demonstrating basic driving skills, obeying road signs, and parking.
- Step 12: If you pass, your permanent DL will be issued within a few days and can be collected at the RTO or delivered to your registered address.
How to Apply for a DL Offline in Haryana
Those who would rather receive help in person can apply offline by going to the RTO:
- Step 1: Find the closest RTO office and pick up Form 1A (Medical Certificate) and Form 2 (Application for Learner's Licence), among other forms.
- Step 2: Complete the application forms accurately, attaching all necessary paperwork, such as identification and proof of address.
- Step 3: Pay the application money in full and send passport-sized photos for verification.
- Step 4: Set up the learner's test date after submitting the documents. The test focuses on safety requirements, driving laws, and road signs.
- Step 5: Your learner's licence will be issued immediately or forwarded to the address you registered if you pass the test.
- Step 6: Get a permanent licence at the RTO by submitting Form 4 after having a learner's licence for at least 30 days. A date for the driving test can also be set at this point.
- Step 7: Show up for the RTO's driving exam, where you must prove your abilities. If you pass, your permanent DL will be issued by the RTO.
Driving Test Procedure in Haryana
To get a permanent driver's licence in Haryana, you must be at least eighteen and have a valid learner's licence (30–180 days). Use your local RTO or the Parivahan Sewa Portal to submit your application with the necessary paperwork and fees. The Regional Transport Office (RTO) requires applicants to take a structured driving exam to show their driving prowess and understanding of traffic laws.
Two-Wheelers and Three-Wheelers Driving Test
Complete a figure-eight pattern without touching the ground, showcasing your accuracy and balance.
- Evaluation of Road Skills: Practice safe driving on public roads by being mindful of your surroundings and following the traffic laws.
Conditions for the Test Day:
- Bring your original driver's licence, certificate of test application receipt, evidence of fee payment, and the vehicle's insurance and registration documents.
- Check that the car is operating well and complies with safety regulations.
The post-test process:
- Results: You will receive quick performance comments from the examiner.
- You have seven days to reapply for the test if you don't pass the first time.
- Licencing: Those who are accepted will get their driver's licence in the mail.
Four-Wheelers Driving Test
- Vehicle Manoeuvres: To show mastery, precision, and control of vehicle handling, execute specific patterns, like the 'H' or 'T.'
- Traffic Driving Assessment: Demonstrate compliance with traffic signs, traffic laws, and general road safety by driving in real-world traffic situations.
- Parking Skills: Show off your mastery of various parking strategies, such as parallel and reverse parking.
Test-Day Prerequisites:
- Bring your original learner's licence, test application acknowledgement receipt, evidence of fee payment, and documents proving your vehicle's registration and insurance.
- The test vehicle must be in top operating condition and fulfil all safety requirements.
Procedure for Post-Test:
- Findings: Get the examiner's response right away.
- Re-Test: You have seven days to wait before reapplying if the test is not cleared.
- Licence Issuance: A successful test ensures your Driving Licence will be sent to you via post.
How to Check Driving Licence Application Status in Haryana
To check the status of your driving licence application in Haryana, follow these steps:
- Step 1: Visit the Sarathi Parivahan Portal: Go to the official Sarathi Parivahan website.
- Step 2: Select Haryana: On the homepage, you'll find a dropdown menu labelled "Select State Name." Choose "Haryana" from the list.
- Step 3: Access Application Status: After selecting Haryana, you'll be redirected to the state's specific portal. Click on the "Application Status" option in the top menu bar.
- Step 4: Enter Necessary Information. Your date of birth and application number will be asked for. Keep these facts close at hand.
- Step 5: Click "Submit" once you've filled out the required fields and checked your status. You will see the status of your application on the screen.
DL Fees in Haryana
The RTO standardises the fees for various driving licence services in Haryana. Here is an outline of the fees:
Eligibility Criteria for Applying for a Driving Licence in Haryana
To apply for a DL in Haryana, specific eligibility requirements must be met, which vary depending on the vehicle type and the type of licence:
Meeting the eligibility criteria is crucial to proceed with the application process for any type of DL, including a Smart Card Driving Licence (DL). A Smart Card Driving Licence (DL) is an upgraded, secure version of the traditional driving licence designed for better durability and data management. Individuals not meeting these criteria cannot apply for a driving licence in Haryana.
Documents Required for Driving Licence Application
In Haryana, the following paperwork must be included with your DL application. The applications for permanent and learner's licences differ slightly in these materials.
Documents Required for a Learner’s Licence:
- Proof of Age (one of the following):
- Birth Certificate
- School Leaving Certificate
- PAN Card
- Passport
Proof of Address (one of the following):
- Voter ID Card
- Aadhaar Card
- Utility Bill (electricity, water, or telephone bill)
- Rental Agreement
- Passport
This form is required for applicants above 50 or those applying for a commercial licence.
Passport-sized Photographs:
Generally, a few copies of recent passport-sized photographs are required for identity verification.
Documents Required for a Permanent Driving Licence:
- Learner’s Licence: The learner’s licence must be at least 30 days old.
- Application Form (Form 4): This is the standard application form for a permanent driving licence.
- Passport-sized Photographs: Recent photographs are usually required for verification.
DL Renewal
To renew your driving licence in Haryana, following the proper procedures and meeting the requirements is essential. Here are the key points to keep in mind:
- Validity of Licence: The validity of a private driving licence is 20 years or until the possessor becomes 50, whichever comes first. Once this time has passed, renewal is required.
Where to File an Application:
- You can apply in person at the closest RTO office.
- Alternatively, for convenience, apply online using the Parivahan Sewa site.
- Documents Necessary:
- driving licence that has expired (original).
- Evidence of age includes a birth certificate, PAN card, or Aadhaar card.
- Utility bills, a rental agreement, or an Aadhaar card are examples of proof of address.
- A medical certificate is required for candidates who are above 50 or who are renewing a business licence.
- recent photo the size of a passport.
- The typical renewal fee is 200 naira. There can be extra costs for services like smart card issuance.
Renewed Licence Validity:
- For those under 50 years: Renewed licence is valid for 10 years.
- For those over 50 years: Validity is reduced to 5 years.
- For commercial licences: Typically valid for 5 years regardless of age.
- Processing Time: Once the application is submitted and approved, the renewed licence is generally issued within a few working days.
Duplicate DL in Haryana
In Haryana, you can apply for a duplicate driver's licence if your original one has been lost, damaged, or vandalised. It entails completing the necessary application stages and submitting specific documentation. What you need to know is as follows:
Documents Required for Duplicate DL
To apply for a duplicate driving licence, you need to provide the following:
- Application Form 2: Complete and submit the Form, which may be found on the Parivahan Sewa portal or at the RTO.
- Original Licence: Send the original licence for verification if it is cracked or substantially defaced.
- Photocopy of Licence: If you have attested copies of your driver's licence, please submit them in case the original is lost.
- Specified Charges: Following the instructions of the Haryana Transport Department, pay the relevant payments, including user costs.
- Proof Cards: Aadhaar cards, PAN cards, and utility bills are examples of supporting documentation for proof of age and address.
You might have to file an FIR or NCR (Non-Cognizable Report) with the local police station if your licence is stolen or misplaced.
How to Apply for a Duplicate DL
- The Regional Transport Office (RTO) is where you should go to get your original licence.
- Gather and complete the application (Form 2).
- You can also go to the Parivahan Sewa website.
- Proceed to the "Driving Licence Services" area and choose "Apply for Duplicate DL."
- Upload scanned copies of your documents and complete the necessary fields.
- Send in your documents:
- All required paperwork should be attached, such as evidence of address, age, and, if relevant, an FIR or NCR.
- Together with the filled-out application form, submit them.
Cover Fees:
- Online or in person at the RTO office, pay the required fees. Make sure you get a receipt for the money you spent.
Verification and Processing:
- The RTO will handle your application and check your documentation.
- It will issue a duplicate DL if the paperwork is in order.
- After being accepted, you can pick up the duplicate DL from the RTO or send it to you by postal service.
- A duplicate driver's licence can be obtained more quickly if your documentation is accurate and comprehensive.

title: e-Ravaana fraud: Three including main accused arrested in Yamunanagar - The Times of India
article_text:
YAMUNANAGAR: The teams of district police arrested three persons, in connection with a case of preparing ‘fake online sale and purchase documents (transit pass) of raw mining material and minerals’ and ‘registering them as genuine on e-Ravaana
Haryana government portal’ in Yamunanagar district.
The police said the arrested accused have been identified as Desh Deepak of Roop Nagar and Gurpreet Singh of Durga Garden, both of Jagadhri, and Anuj Kumar of Kotdi village in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh.
“All three accused were produced in the district court on Saturday, which sent Desh Deepak and Anuj Kumar on 7-day police remand, while Gurpreet was sent to judicial custody”, said Yamunanagar police spokesman.
He said that on the directions of SP Mohit Handa, the teams of CIA-II and Pratap Nagar police station arrested three persons, as they prepared fake bills of purchase of ‘illegally mined minerals’ of other states and registered them on e-Ravana portal of mining and geology department (MGD), Haryana, to show them as genuine purchase.
On September 14, mining officer (MO) Rajesh Sangwan lodged a complaint against a screening plant at a village in Yamunanagar, after which, a case was registered under Section 120-B (criminal conspiracy), 379 (theft) and 420 (cheating) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and 21 (5) of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation of Development) Act at Pratap Nagar police station in Yamunanagar.
It was stated in his complaint by the MO that an inspection was conducted at a screening plant at a village on September 13, and it came to light that this plant was closed eight months ago. However, the owners of this plant were creating online purchase and sale documents of raw mining material and processed minerals, respectively, against their mineral dealer license (MDL) linked to e-Ravana portal of MGD, Haryana government, said the MO.
“Upon checking e-Ravana portal of the said screening plant, it came to light that another firm (involved in stone crushing) purchased mining material through 171 e-ravana bills on July 23, 2022, while as per the NGT (National Green Tribunal), the mining operations in the quarry (of Yamuna) was closed from July 1 to September 15”, said MO Rajesh.
As per sources, the above fact proved that the accused screening plant owners did not make any purchase of raw mining material and sold processed minerals including sand, stone, gravel, etc., but for their monetary benefits, they sold their fake documents of sale and purchase of mining material to a stone crusher owners, who allegedly undertake illegal mining on the basis of concerned fake online documents to get cheaper raw mining material.
The information said that accused screening plant owners not only caused loss to the state exchequer by misusing the departmental portal, but also showed illegal mining as genuine through fake e-Ravana documents and affected the environment by carrying out illegal mining.
